notes:
Topline: mid-market analytics SaaS (product analytics + in-app assistants) evaluating Redwood Hosted API initially; now moving to Dedicated POC. Short, bullet-style CRM notes below.

- Contact(s): VP Product - Nina Patel, Head of Infra - Omar Kline, ML Lead - Tasha Reynolds.
- Use-case summary: customer-facing help assistant + in-app insight summaries + relevance reranking for search results. Heavy embedding footprint for semantic search (daily batch + near-real-time refresh).
- Perf targets: p50 token latency < 120ms for short-chat requests, p95 < 300ms; throughput target ~80-120 reqs/sec during peak; embedding refresh window 15min.
- Cost sensitivity: mid/high — wants predictable committed pricing; exploring reserved capacity for predictable unit economics. Estimated ARR justifies Dedicated commit if unit cost reduction >= 30%.
- Model preference: open model family (Llama/Redwood-verified variants) for cost control + ability to pin quantized variants. Also interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching.
- Security: must have SSO/SAML, audit logging, customer-managed KMS, and data residency in NA (no EU processing). Legal insists on SOC2 + retention controls.
- Deployment ask: initial Hosted API PoC demonstrated feature parity. Next step is a 2-week Dedicated POC in our test VPC: replicate production traffic profile, enable canary routing to a small % of traffic, and validate fallback/rollback mechanics.
- Canary plan (high level):
  * Week 1: deploy Dedicated model variant (quantized) to a canary pool (5-10% traffic). Route by traffic tag from a staging route. Monitor latency, error rate, and token cost.
  * Health gates: no >2x error rate vs hosted baseline, p95 latency within 1.5x, no quality regressions on eval prompt set.
  * Week 2: ramp to 30% then 60% if gates pass. Verify KV/prefix cache behavior and autoscale.
  * Fallbacks: automatic fallback to Hosted API model family in other region (us-west) on rate/latency/error thresholds; manual rollback playbook validated with SE.
- Routing requirements: request-level routing by policy (latency-first for web chat, cost-first for batch reranking), model variant mapping for compatibility. Must support region failover (us-east -> us-west) and cross-region cache warmup plan.
- Observability ask: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency heatmaps, and end-to-end trace for failed requests. Redwood Console screens demo'd were well received.
- POC success criteria: 1) performance parity within SLOs, 2) >25% cost reduction compared to Hosted for steady-state batch workload, 3) validated canary + rollback without user-visible errors, 4) legal sign-off on residencies/retention.
- Pricing negotiation: asked for 12-month reserved capacity quote and a staged ramp discount. AE has a pricing sheet; finance needs one more iteration.
- Quotes from calls: "Need predictable unit cost — we can only commit if we can forecast ops costs to within 10%" — Nina P.

Recent friction: legal requested sample audit logs and encryption certs; networking needs a list of IPs for VPC allowlist. SE (Diego) to produce runbook for VPC peering + test harness.

Next operational items (owner tags):
- Diego: Provide Dedicated POC runbook + canary gate checklist (due: 2024-11-20).
- Arielle (AE): Get final pricing term sheet and submit to LucidGrove finance (due: 2024-11-22).
- Legal: review data residency clause after receiving security FAQ (pending).

Notes style: fragments, shorthand, and action-oriented bullets to match internal CRM.
